Second-source situation is general rather than per-specimen: nl.wikipedia's Arboretum Trompenburg article and the International Oak Society's page on the garden both confirm Trompenburg holds the Dutch National Plant Collection of Quercus (oak) and is internationally known for oak breeding (named hybrids raised there include Quercus 'Pondaim' and Q. x rosacea 'East Column'/'West Column'), but neither names this individual evergreen oak, so this is flagged rather than a clean two-independent-source pass on the specific tree. Garden background for the writer: laid out from 1820 by James Smith, who combined the estate with neighbouring land in 1859; the western section redesigned around 1870 by father-and-son landscape architects Jan David and Louis Paul Zocher; turned into a true arboretum by James van Hoey Smith after roughly 400 elms were felled to Dutch elm disease in 1928; developed into an internationally recognised collection by his son Dick van Hoey Smith; opened to the public in 1958; received the International Dendrology Society's Conservation Plaquette in 1983.
